annotations.text: We combine repeated evaluations, controlled task variations, and lifecycle interventions to examine whether improvements from skill evolution persist and transfer, and to trace their origins to feedback, revision, selection, skill content, and evaluation.
annotations.comment: 摘要替换：围绕改进能否保持、迁移及其来源合并实验概述；替换原版 Across SkillRevise 开头的方法枚举句。

annotations.text: We organize the experiments around utility, behavioral scope, and lifecycle attribution. Repeated standard-task evaluations of SkillEvolver, SPARK, and CoEvoSkills measure skill utility, and controlled task variants examine how far that utility extends. Inspection of skill content and execution traces then identifies reusable decisions expressed during deployment. Complementary mechanism studies in SkillRevise, SkillHone, and SkillOpt examine retention and the origins of observed gains. These studies represent trace-conditioned revision, history-based iterative honing, and validation-gated bounded editing in frozen-agent systems with persistent external skill artifacts.
annotations.comment: 引言替换：说明标准任务、变体评估、技能复用分析与后续机制研究的关系。

annotations.text: Skill Utility and Reuse on SkillsBench We first ask whether completed skills help on their source tasks, then whether that utility extends when the tasks change. Repeated standard-task evaluations establish the observed benefit of deploying the final artifacts. Controlled variants examine their scope of reuse, and inspection of skill content and execution traces connects these outcomes to the decisions made during deployment.

annotations.text: Experimental Setup We evaluate SkillEvolver (Zhang et al. 2026a), SPARK (Zhou et al. 2026b), and CoEvoSkills (Zhang et al. 2026b) on SkillsBench (Li et al. 2026), with two runs per method. Each run pairs an execution using the generated or evolved skill with a no-skill execution of the same task. Both runs of each method use the same task set: 81 tasks for SkillEvolver, 84 for SPARK, and 85 for CoEvoSkills. annotations.text: Do Completed Skills Help on Their Source Tasks? All three methods achieve positive mean paired gains in both runs (Table 1). SkillEvolver gains 25.61 and 25.02 points, with 27 versus six improved/regressed tasks in run 1 and 26 versus three in run 2. CoEvoSkills gains 10.24 and 9.76 points, with 17 improved tasks in each run and nine versus ten regressions. For these two methods, the paired gains remain similar even though absolute baseline rewards differ between runs. SPARK has smaller positive gains of 1.84 and 6.45 points. Its first run has nearly balanced improvements and regres- sions (nine versus eight); the second has 13 improvements and five regressions. Thus, observing a positive mean gain twice can accompany different patterns of task-level benefit. The repeated positive direction establishes a consistent ag- gregate pattern across the two runs for each method. The co- existence of improvements, regressions, and ties also shows that skill utility varies across tasks. These paired comparisons establish the observed source-task utility of the completed ar- tifacts. They provide the starting point for the reuse question:

annotations.text: Do Evolved Skills Remain Useful When Tasks Change? A source-task skill may capture a reusable procedure, a deci- sion rule, or assumptions specific to that instance. We deploy these skills on controlled variants while keeping each artifact frozen (Figure 2). The executor interprets the changed task and decides how to use the existing skill. Its reward differ- ence from a no-skill execution of the same variant measures the final artifact’s utility under that change.
annotations.comment: 新增变体评估：冻结源任务技能，检验 P1／P2／P3 下的效用及总体结果。

annotations.text: Three forms of task change. Input-representation changes (P1) alter how the task is presented, including names, column arrangements, or schemas. They test whether the executor can recover the relevant roles of the inputs while using the skill. Task-instance changes (P2) replace the data or instance structure. They test whether the procedure can be instantiated with new values rather than relying on a solution specific to the source instance. Coupled-requirement changes (P3) al- ter or add requirements that must be handled together. They test whether the executor can adapt the procedure while pre- serving the constraints that determine a valid output. These changes probe different aspects of reuse rather than succes- sive levels of difficulty.
annotations.comment: 新增变体评估：冻结源任务技能，检验 P1／P2／P3 下的效用及总体结果。

annotations.text: The record contains 222 task variants and 886 condition- level results across no skill and the three methods. Ta- ble 2 summarizes historical and recovery evaluations for 222 SkillEvolver variants and 221 each for SPARK and Co- EvoSkills. Panel B separates the within-variant differences by type of change.

annotations.text: Overall utility under task variation. SkillEvolver in- creases mean reward from 41.87 to 53.81, a gain of 11.94 points, with 47 improved and 20 regressed variants. Thus, its source-task skills retain positive average utility after the tasks change. SPARK increases mean reward from 41.61 to 42.25, a gain of 0.65 points, with 32 improvements and 37 regressions. The positive mean alongside more regressions than improvements reflects the magnitudes of the reward changes: the mean and the number of benefited variants cap- ture different properties. CoEvoSkills decreases mean reward from 41.61 to 36.60, a change of −5.01 points, with 26 im- provements and 41 regressions. Its positive source-task gains therefore coexist with negative average utility on the recorded variants.
annotations.comment: 新增变体评估：冻结源任务技能，检验 P1／P2／P3 下的效用及总体结果。

annotations.text: What the combined results reveal. All three methods ob- tain positive mean gains in both standard-task runs, yet their variant profiles differ substantially. Success on the source tasks and usefulness after task changes are distinct empirical properties. SkillEvolver provides the clearest positive reuse pattern in these records, whereas SPARK’s benefit depends on the type of change and CoEvoSkills’ source-task benefit does not extend on average. Approximately seven in ten vari- ants remain tied with the baseline for each method. The gains therefore arise from a subset of changed outcomes, motivat- ing a closer examination of the decisions expressed when a skill helps or hinders execution.
annotations.comment: 新增分析：不同变化下的效用范围，以及诊断规则和正确性约束如何参与技能复用。

annotations.text: What Is Preserved When a Skill Is Reused? To interpret the variant results, we inspect the skill artifacts together with their execution traces. We distinguish the pro- cedure stored in a skill from the way an executor applies it to a new task. A script can preserve an action sequence, while successful reuse also depends on recognizing when that sequence applies, adjusting its inputs, and checking its output. Figure 3 organizes the inspected evidence around these decisions.
annotations.comment: 新增分析：不同变化下的效用范围，以及诊断规则和正确性约束如何参与技能复用。

annotations.text: Diagnostic rules guide adaptation. In the inspected SkillEvolver artifacts, intermediate checks guide the choice and revision of a procedure. Candidate discovery, diagnosis, and refinement appear as separate operations, with conditions explaining when to revisit an intermediate result. This struc- ture gives the executor opportunities to respond to changed
annotations.comment: 新增分析：不同变化下的效用范围，以及诊断规则和正确性约束如何参与技能复用。

annotations.text: inputs before committing to an output. In the signal-detection traces, for example, the executor uses diagnostic checks to distinguish competing candidate explanations and adjusts the search accordingly. The reusable content is the rule for eval- uating a candidate; the candidate values and search settings can change with the task.
annotations.comment: 新增分析：不同变化下的效用范围，以及诊断规则和正确性约束如何参与技能复用。

annotations.text: Correctness constraints survive solution changes. A second form of reusable content specifies which properties the output must preserve. The inspected scheduling skill ex- presses constraints relative to the supplied instance and base- line, allowing the executor to construct a different schedule while checking the same repair requirements. Failure traces make this distinction visible: much of a workflow can execute correctly while one omitted requirement invalidates the final result. This helps explain why preserving a familiar proce- dure is insufficient when a variant changes how inputs are represented or how requirements interact.
annotations.comment: 新增分析：不同变化下的效用范围，以及诊断规则和正确性约束如何参与技能复用。

annotations.text: Reuse combines preserved rules with new execution. Across the inspected cases, successful adaptation preserves decision criteria and correctness checks while changing input handling, search choices, or the constructed solution. This illustrates how a transferred artifact can help the executor decide what to retain and what to recompute. SkillEvolver’s positive profile across P1–P3 is consistent with this form of reuse. The trace evidence identifies concrete instances of that behavior. Complementary interventions on SkillRevise, SkillHone, and SkillOpt later in the paper test component effects within their respective artifact lineages. The variant evaluations characterize how far final-skill utility extends beyond the source task. The following reten- tion and lifecycle studies examine whether improvements persist under fresh deployment and which parts of the evolu- tion process produce them.
annotations.comment: 新增分析：不同变化下的效用范围，以及诊断规则和正确性约束如何参与技能复用。
